text:
mina: Heads up — seeing a spike of SAML assertion replay-detection alerts for tenant `acme-prod`. Started ~03:58 UTC after the KMS rewrap. Can someone triage?

security-bot: [ALERT] 1765004322 replay-detect count=67 tenant=acme-prod rule=assertion-id-cache-hit severity=medium

aj: On it. Do we have the audit/IdP proxy logs (AuthProxy) for 03:50-04:10? Suspect old assertions being accepted.

sam: Quick checklist: check IdP InResponseTo/MessageID duplication, verify assertion NotOnOrAfter, check KMS rewrap timestamps and whether any service that signs assertions used the old key.

mina: grabbing logs now. sample log lines below (redacted):
```
2026-03-22T03:59:02Z AuthProxy verify assertion-id=3f9a2b0c-... tenant=acme-prod result=ok key-alias=projects/keys/prod-2026-v2
2026-03-22T04:00:11Z AuthProxy verify assertion-id=3f9a2b0c-... tenant=acme-prod result=replay_detected cache-hit=true
2026-03-22T04:01:05Z KMS rewrap key=projects/keys/prod-2026 old=proj-key-2024 new=proj-key-2026 status=success
```

jess: Wait — we rotated the signing key but didn't block acceptance of the previous key for a short window. Could the proxy be rewrapping or re-signing using the old material?

aj: I ran a grep across proxies: `kubectl logs -lapp=auth-proxy -n prod | grep 3f9a2b0c` — found identical assertion-id used across 8 requests from different source IPs within 90s. Looks like replay, not duplicate submission.

oncall: Assigning priority P1 for visible customer impact. @infra @idp-team please join. Mitigation: throttle/blacklist assertion-id hits and add temporary WAF rule to drop identical assertion-id within 5m.

sam: Also check SCIM/webhook consumers — if a provisioning job retried and replayed an old assertion to the IdP (weird but possible) it could surface as repeated assertions. Any recent RBAC changes that might have changed the job identity?

mina: FYI there was an RBAC change yesterday that gave the provisioner service account `impersonate` perms to exec a login flow for backfilled accounts. I'll dump recent IAM binds.

security-bot: [KMS] 2026-03-22T03:58:59Z rewrap initiated by: automation/rotations scheduled-by=key-owner service=key-rotation-runner

aj: Two-prong triage: 1) short-term mitigation = WAF/rate-limit assertions with identical assertion-id + blackhole by tenant. 2) gather forensic traces: all proxy logs, KMS audit, provisioning job logs, and SCIM request logs for 03:45-04:15.

mina: Forensics: running queries now. Command I'm using: `gcloud logging read "resource.labels.project_id=\"redwood-prod\" AND (\"acme-prod\" OR \"3f9a2b0c\") AND timestamp>\"2026-03-22T03:45:00Z\"" --format=json`

sam: Check the assertion attributes too — if NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter window was too wide or clock skew on IdP vs SP could make old assertions accepted. Add a search for `NotOnOrAfter >= 2026-03-22T04:05:00Z`.

jess: Could be a signing key race: we rotated the key, but the verification path still accepted both old and new key material for a minute. If an attacker captured an assertion (or a misbehaving job replays it), they'd succeed during that overlap.

mina: Quick mitigation applied: increased strictness on replay cache to 10m for tenant acme-prod and pushed a temporary WAF drop rule. I'll monitor. :thumbsup:

oncall: Good. Also open an incident (INC-2026-0347) and notify legal/customer-success for acme-prod. We need to follow disclosure playbook if data exposure confirmed.

aj: Evidence so far leans replay from internal job vs external attack: source IPs cluster to our provisioning runners, and KMS logs show rewrap at 03:58 then a spike of requests from prov-runner-1 between 03:59-04:02.

mina: Copying relevant snippet from provisioning job logs: `2026-03-22T03:59:00Z provisioner backfill account=acct-123 action=login_simulate assertion-id=3f9a2b0c retries=3` — looks like an automated retry loop.

sam: If prov job is reusing a cached assertion (bad), we need a code fix: always fetch fresh assertion per login attempt, avoid reusing previously stored SAML response. Patch + rollback plan?

jess: Agreed. For next steps: 1) patch provisioner to fetch new auth (PR in review), 2) backfill mitigation: revoke session tokens created after 03:58 for affected accounts, 3) postmortem and update rotation playbook to ensure no overlap acceptance window.

mina: I'll coordinate the patch + revoke + customer comms. Adding runbook checklist to the incident.

security-bot: [AUDIT] incident INC-2026-0347 created by oncall. Artifacts: auth-proxy-logs.zip, kms-audit.csv, prov-logs.zip attached.

oncall: Assign owners: mina (triage/mitigation), aj (forensics), sam (fix/patch). ETA for mitigation complete = 30m.

mina: Mitigation in place, replay count dropping to 0 over last 3 intervals. Still collecting logs for full scope.

aj: Forensic note: no evidence of external IPs outside our fleet. Marking as internal automation misconfiguration. Recommend urgent audit of all provisioning jobs that were granted impersonation during last RBAC change.

jess: I'll schedule a short vuln triage to see if this pattern could be abused or if any CVE-like disclosure needed.

mina: Closing loop later today with postmortem. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
